articles.summary: Several Bank Rakyat pages, including the iRakyat login, were defaced late on 6 November by an actor calling itself MARLANWG, and the bank pulled most sites offline. The bank has not confirmed a breach or data exposure; the minister said the affected site was run by a third party.
articles.title: Bank Rakyat Takes Down Sites After Suspected Cyber Attack

articles.summary: Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said on 12 November that NACSA remains at amber alert, a moderate readiness level. Claims of attacks and intrusions are circulating online, but NACSA has confirmed none so far and will be the official source of information.
articles.title: Nacsa maintains amber alert amid cyberattack, security breach claims

articles.summary: The Star reports on the widening cyber risk picture after NACSA lifted the national threat level to medium on 4 November, with critical-infrastructure sector heads now submitting weekly threat status reports to the agency.
articles.title: Malaysia facing increasingly complex cybersecurity risks

articles.summary: The Election Commission says its website was reportedly attacked during the Melaka state election and it is still waiting for a full report. Chairman Ramlan Harun said an initial report went to the authorities and the commission is working with MCMC. The nature of the attack and any data impact are not yet disclosed.
articles.title: Election Commission Claims Cyberattack On Its Website

articles.summary: The National Security Council said the cyber situation remains under control after incidents and disruptions at several financial institutions. NACSA's NC4 is monitoring, sector leads and critical-infrastructure operators are working with it, and Bank Negara leads the financial sector response. The public was told to ignore unverified attack claims and use official channels.
articles.title: National cybersecurity situation under control, threat level moderate, says MKN

articles.summary: NACSA reported 5,110 cyber incidents in Malaysia between January and September 2026. The figure was released days after the national threat level moved from Low to Medium on 4 November, and it frames the warnings from the Prime Minister about hybrid attacks.
articles.title: Nacsa records 5,110 cyber incidents in Malaysia from January to September

articles.summary: Czech scraping platform Apify, with about 91,000 customers, said an intruder using a compromised credential accessed customer accounts on 9 and 10 November. It confirmed on 12 November that personal data and stored data were reached, revoked some OAuth connections and is still investigating.
articles.title: Apify Confirms Customer Data Accessed in Cyberattack

articles.summary: Researchers say a campaign dubbed wfx-loot began on 10 November, using stolen valid tokens to probe over 61,000 repositories and plant credential-stealing code in CI workflows and npm hooks. Aikido saw execution in more than 1,800 repositories; teams are advised to rotate exposed secrets.
articles.title: Attacker Targets 60,000 GitHub Repositories in Credential Theft Campaign

articles.summary: Norway's aid agency Norad confirmed on 5 November that attackers abusing 27 accounts took names and emails of all 20,614 Grants Portal users, plus documents from three foreign organisations. The national security authority sees similarities with other recent attacks; no group has claimed it.
articles.title: Norwegian aid agency hit by cyberattack exposing data of 20K users

articles.region: Japan, Singapore, Hong Kong & South Korea
articles.summary: Japan Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Singapore Airlines, Korean Air, Asiana and Malaysia Airlines disclosed passenger data exposure traced to reservation provider Amadeus. Reported counts include 92,000 at JAL, 53,000 at Cathay and 46,000 at Singapore Airlines. Amadeus says a booking-display vulnerability was fixed and it found no payment data accessed.
articles.title: Asian airlines announce data breaches tied to IT provider incident (Amadeus)

articles.summary: On 9 November Paris prosecutors and ANSSI attributed the 12 October attack on about 700 French supermarkets to the IRGC-linked Shahid Kaveh group. Refrigeration reached 50C for hours. France summoned the Iranian ambassador and promised EU sanctions, and similar incidents were reported in several other European countries.
articles.title: France Blames Iran for a Cyberattack That Heated Supermarket Refrigerators

articles.summary: Thailand's deputy transport minister instructed aviation agencies and businesses that maintain public databases to tighten security after airline breaches across Asia. Thai Airways disclosed on 9 November that about 60,000 booking records may have been accessed through its supplier's system, without affecting its own systems or card data.
articles.title: Thailand orders tighter aviation cyber security after data breaches across Asia

articles.summary: Home Minister Saifuddin Nasution told the Dewan Rakyat on 12 November that a breach of house-arrest conditions would revoke the order and return Najib to Kajang Prison. Three prison officers per shift guard the residence at no extra cost, drawn from Kajang Prison staff.
articles.title: Najib could go back to prison if he breaches terms of house arrest, Dewan Rakyat told

articles.summary: Business Today summarises Parliament's sixth week: the house-arrest terms barring Najib from leaving the premises, politics and media, plus debate on national debt and GST. House arrest runs to 23 August 2028, and the Bar has sought judicial review of the Pardons Board decision.
articles.title: Najib House Arrest Conditions, National Debt And GST Dominate Parliament's Sixth Week

milestones.label: Dewan Rakyat Budget 2027 committee-stage debates resume
Dewan Rakyat starts government bills including AG and Public Prosecutor split

articles.summary: Budget 2027 committee-stage debates continue 16 to 19 November, after which seven bills take the floor from 30 November, including the Constitution (Amendment) (No. 2) Bill splitting the AG and Public Prosecutor roles. The session ends on 8 December; the list may change.
articles.title: Seven bills lined up for Dewan Rakyat from Nov 30

articles.summary: Early voting for the Melaka state election on 10 November saw 94.96 percent turnout, with 9,417 of 9,917 eligible security-force voters casting ballots. Polling day for the 28 assembly seats, contested by 79 candidates, is Saturday 14 November.
articles.title: Melaka polls: Early voter turnout at 94.96%

milestones.label: Court of Appeal case management in Sabah 40 percent revenue appeal

articles.summary: In the federal government's appeal over Sabah's 40 percent revenue entitlement, the Court of Appeal used 12 November case management to fix a further session on 1 December. No ruling date or judgment has been reported; an earlier stay still pauses the High Court timelines.
articles.title: 40pc: Further case management fixed for December 1

articles.summary: Government spokesman Fahmi Fadzil said the Cabinet, chaired by Anwar, agreed a Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry memorandum on 6 November, described as a step towards Sarawak's environmental autonomy under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 arrangements.
articles.title: Cabinet agrees memorandum on Sarawak environmental autonomy under MA63

articles.summary: On 3 November the Court of Appeal allowed lawyer Mahajoth Singh to start judicial review of two orders the MACC issued against him, a case testing the limits of the anti-graft agency's investigative powers.
articles.title: Court Of Appeal Grants Lawyer Mahajoth Singh Leave To Challenge MACC Orders

milestones.label: Court of Appeal case management in Rosmah solar graft appeal

articles.summary: The Court of Appeal had allowed Rosmah Mansor on 1 September to introduce additional evidence in her appeal against conviction and sentence in the solar hybrid graft case, then stayed that order pending a Federal Court appeal. The Court of Appeal fixed case management for 25 November, with a further mention on 3 December.
articles.title: Rosmah's bid to introduce fresh evidence in solar graft case held up by Federal Court appeal

articles.fixedIn: Upgrade to OpenSSH 10.6p2 (Alpine packages shipped 5 Nov) and restart sshd; otherwise disable password authentication.

response.text: Build a playbook that queries the asset inventory and XSIAM endpoint data for Alpine or musl-based hosts and containers running sshd below 10.6p2. It opens a ticket per host with owner and exposure. Analysts approve restarts of production sshd.
response.title: Find musl SSH hosts

response.text: Run an XQL query over auth and sshd logs for successful password logins to Alpine hosts from new source IPs, especially after very long password attempts. The analyst gets a ranked host list. Treat any hit as a compromise and isolate after approval.
response.title: Hunt anomalous SSH logins

response.text: Setting PasswordAuthentication no in sshd_config and restricting port 22 with firewall rules removes the attack path without building automation. Do this before the package upgrade window. Verify with an external scan.
response.title: Disable password auth

response.prompt: List hosts and container images running Alpine or other musl libc with OpenSSH sshd below 10.6p2 and password authentication enabled. Rank by internet exposure, include owner and last login anomalies, and recommend patch or mitigation per host in max 10 bullets.
response.text: Ask the Cortex AI assistant to summarise exposed Alpine and musl hosts from incident data. It lists images, owners and priorities. Analysts validate against the vendor advisory.
response.title: Alpine exposure triage

articles.summary: Portable OpenSSH before 10.6p2 on Linux with musl libc and no PAM, such as Alpine, lets attackers log in with an oversized password. Attacks began within hours of publication in early November and CISA added it to KEV on 9 November.

articles.fixedIn: Upgrade IBM Aspera Faspex to 5.0.19 PL1 on Linux and verify the faspex-core container image; no workaround.

response.text: Create a playbook that finds Faspex 5 servers in the CMDB or vulnerability data, compares versions with 5.0.19 PL1 and checks internet exposure. It opens prioritised tickets. Analysts approve upgrade windows.
response.title: Faspex version sweep

response.text: Use an automation to pull Faspex user and role changes since 1 November and flag accounts promoted to administrator. The analyst gets a diff per server. Any unexplained promotion is escalated as a possible compromise.
response.title: Audit new Faspex admins

response.text: XSIAM Vulnerability and Exposure Management can track this CVE across agent-covered endpoints without custom playbooks. Use it to see affected hosts and assign work. Add a firewall restriction on Faspex while patching.
response.title: Use Emerging Vulnerabilities view

response.prompt: Summarise IBM Aspera Faspex 5 servers below 5.0.19 PL1, whether internet-facing, and any user promoted to administrator since 2026-11-01. Rank by risk and propose containment steps needing analyst approval, max 10 bullets.
response.text: Ask the Cortex AI assistant for a short summary of Faspex hosts and suspicious admin changes. It gives analysts a patch order. Validate against IBM bulletin.
response.title: Faspex exposure summary

articles.summary: IBM patched an incorrect-authorization flaw in Faspex 5.0.0 to 5.0.19 on 7 November that lets an authenticated user gain administrator rights, rated 9.8 by IBM. CISA added it to KEV on 9 November with a 12 November deadline.

articles.fixedIn: No fix stated; N-able restricted the Legacy API and Intune integration, and hotfix 2026.4 HF2 alone is reported insufficient.

response.text: Build a playbook that lists N-central servers, checks whether the Legacy API is enabled and whether the web interface is internet reachable. It then searches for unknown scripts and XMRig processes. Analysts approve disabling the API.
response.title: N-central exposure and IOC check

response.text: Run an XQL query for XMRig or unusual high-CPU processes and new scheduled scripts on N-central hosts and on managed endpoints. The analyst gets a host list. Isolate confirmed hits only after approval.
response.title: Hunt for miners on servers

response.text: Blocking internet access to N-central and turning off the Legacy API is faster than any new automation and removes the reported attack path. Re-enable only for required partners. Check vendor guidance before restoring.
response.title: Restrict access at the firewall

response.prompt: Draft a compromise assessment checklist for an N-able N-central server suspected of exploitation via the 4EverAble2Shell chain and CVE-2026-90436. Include log sources, persistence, miner indicators, managed-agent impact and evidence to preserve, max 12 bullets.
response.text: Ask the Cortex AI assistant to draft a compromise assessment for an N-central server. It lists logs and artefacts to preserve. Analysts verify with the vendor and Huntress guidance.
response.title: Compromise assessment

articles.summary: A proof of concept published on 12 November chains an Apache Axis bug (CVE-2026-90436, CVSS 9.8) with an N-central flaw for unauthenticated root code execution when the Legacy API is enabled. Attacks began within hours, reportedly against fully patched servers; no fix was stated.
